1	---
2	name: handoff-format
3	description: "Layout and templates for sdlc-lite task folders (.sdlc/<task>/) and handoff files. Reference for the launcher skills; not a command."
4	user-invocable: false
5	---
6	
7	**Codex host:** Before following this workflow, read [the Codex adapter](../sdlc-lite/SKILL.md) and apply its tool, argument, path, and process translations. Claude Code follows the workflow below directly.
8	
9	## Layout
10	
11	```
12	.sdlc/<task-slug>/
13	  handoff.md            task brief (goal, intent, context, constraints)
14	  design.md             /grill ratified design (optional)
15	  decompose/            /decompose manifest-v<n>.json + report.md (optional)
16	  scout-L1.md           outputs of task-level roles: <role>-<level>.md
17	  planner-L2.md
18	  planner-L3-2.md       a replan; the latest runs.jsonl record is current
19	  plan-reviewer-L1.md   plan review (planner L3, a step at L4 or L5, a merge step, or a replan)
20	  runs.jsonl            one line per run: role, level, model, effort, cost, duration, file
21	  skips.md              lane history: one "- lane:" line per steps.py lane run, under ## Lane
22	                        and, under ## Skipped, one entry per full-chain role (planner, verifier
23	                        per step, filer) a solo, lean, or fix lane skipped (a full lane
24	                        needs the results instead), in the form
25	                        "- skip: <role>; step: <n or all>; reason: <why>; decided: <who>"
26	                        (reason and decided non-empty); tickets.py check and close enforce it
27	  step-1/
28	    handoff.md          one plan step: level, do, acceptance criteria
29	    builder-L2.md
30	    verifier-L1.md
31	  step-2/ ...
32	  step-2.superseded-1/   a step replaced by a replan; ignored as a step, still counted for cost
33	.sdlc/.NNNN-<slug>/     a closed ticket in numbered mode (renamed from NNNN-<slug> by `close`, which refuses while other files cite the old path unless `--rewrite-refs` or `--force`); same layout inside
34	.sdlc/roadmap.md        generated by `tickets.py roadmap`; never hand-edited
35	.sdlc/notes.md          follow-ups that did not become tickets, appended by `tickets.py close`; never a ticket
36	.sdlc/_templates/<type>.md  optional; overrides the plugin's skills/ticket/templates/<type>.md
37	.sdlc/AGENTS.md         router: stage counts, open tickets, and the create, claim, and close procedures; its managed block is regenerated by tickets.py roadmap, new, and close
38	.sdlc/CLAUDE.md         @AGENTS.md, so Claude Code loads the router
39	.sdlc/config            optional lines: ticket_folders: numbered, external_branch: <branch>, ticket_root: tickets
40	.sdlc/tickets/          the ticket folders when config has ticket_root: tickets, with its own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; roadmap.md, notes.md, config, and _templates/ stay in .sdlc/
41	.sdlc/runtime/          traces analysis outputs and cursor written by `traces.py` (runtime/traces/<repo-key>/); never committed
42	.sdlc/messages/         git-ignored mailbox written by scripts/messages.py: new/, read/, done/ per receiver, shared by worktrees; never committed; its AGENTS.md (the procedures) and CLAUDE.md at the root and in each stage folder are written by messages.py send and tickets.py roadmap
43	.sdlc/evals/            the plugin repository's dated model and effort evals (NNNN-<slug>.md) and table-lock.json, written by scripts/evals.py add and lock; check.py fails a model-table change that cites no newer eval; its AGENTS.md documents the format
44	.sdlc/proposals/        candidate changes mined from past runs (<kind>-<hash>/proposal.md, P-NNNN), written by scripts/proposals.py scan; accept needs an eval in .sdlc/evals/, promote files an idea ticket; its AGENTS.md documents the format
45	.sdlc/supervisor/       written by `supervisor.py init` in the main checkout: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, limits.json; hosts.local.json, state.json, status.json, lock, STOP, and wakes/ stay local
46	```
47	
48	`scripts/run.sh <role> <level> <handoff.md>` writes `<role>-<level>.md` and `.log` next to the handoff it is given. A rerun of the same role and level writes `<role>-<level>-<k>.md` and `.log` (k = 2, 3, ...); the first result is never overwritten, and the newest is decided by `scripts/order.py`: latest runs.jsonl record (run.sh records `file`), else level then rerun index then name; never mtime. runs.jsonl keeps the history. Add `.sdlc/` to the project's `.gitignore` unless the user wants the trail committed.
49	
50	A live step dir is exactly `step-<digits>`; a replan renames replaced dirs to `step-<n>.superseded-<k>/` (k is the first free number); the board and scripts do not count these as steps.
51	
52	If the project commits the `.sdlc/` trail, ignore these instead so `/board` and role runs don't dirty the tree:
53	
54	```
55	.sdlc/**/*.running
56	.sdlc/**/*.log
57	.sdlc/**/.run.lock
58	.sdlc/runtime/
59	.sdlc/messages/
60	.sdlc/supervisor/hosts.local.json
61	.sdlc/supervisor/status.json
62	.sdlc/supervisor/state.json
63	.sdlc/supervisor/lock
64	.sdlc/supervisor/STOP
65	.sdlc/supervisor/wakes/
66	```
67	
68	- Board cache: lives in `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/sdlc-lite/board-state/`, outside the repo, so `/board` writes nothing into the tree. Ignoring `.sdlc/.board-state.json` only matters for older versions that wrote it there.
69	- `.sdlc/**/*.running`: marker for a role run in progress
70	- `.sdlc/**/*.log`: raw role transcript (stream-json: one JSON event per line, stderr mixed in)
71	- `.sdlc/**/.run.lock`: local lock state used to prevent overlapping runs
72	- `.sdlc/runtime/`: `traces.py` analysis outputs and ingest cursor, regenerated on each run
73	- `.sdlc/messages/`: the local mailbox written by `scripts/messages.py`; never committed, even when the trail is.
74	
75	Keep the results `.md` files, `runs.jsonl`, and `*.attempt.json` committed. Attempt records preserve failed and interrupted runs even when no normal run row was written.
76	
77	## Ticket front matter (optional)
78	
79	In numbered mode, `close` renames the folder `NNNN-<slug>` to `.NNNN-<slug>`; tools still treat it as a closed ticket. Before the rename, `close` refuses, writing nothing, when files outside the folder cite `<root>/NNNN-<slug>` (found with `git grep`), naming each; `--rewrite-refs` rewrites them to the dot path with the rename, and `--force` closes and leaves them.
80	
81	`.sdlc/<task>/handoff.md` may open with a YAML front matter block that makes the handoff double as a ticket:
82	
83	```
84	---
85	id: T-NNNN
86	title: "..."
87	type: feature|bug|chore|spike|idea
88	status: proposed|ready|blocked|done|dropped
89	size: S|M|L|XL
90	priority: P1|P2|P3
91	depends: [T-NNNN, file:<path>, cap:<name>, ...]
92	created: YYYY-MM-DD
93	from: T-NNNN   # optional, origin ticket id
94	provides: [name, ...]   # optional, capability names this ticket delivers
95	claimed_by: <harness> <YYYY-MM-DD>   # optional, who works on it; shown in the router; a second claimant checks it first
96	router: .sdlc/AGENTS.md   # stamped by new: the folder rules (.sdlc/tickets/AGENTS.md with ticket_root: tickets)
97	---
98	```
99	
100	A `file:` depends entry is repo-relative and met once the path exists; it never orders tickets. A `cap:` entry is met once a `done` ticket provides it, and orders the ticket after every provider. `check` fails a malformed entry or an unprovided `cap:`.
101	
102	Front matter is purely additive: a handoff with no front matter keeps working unchanged, and `run.sh` never requires or parses it. `board.py` reads `id`/`status` from front matter for display only (via `tickets.py`'s parser, so a task without front matter or an unreadable handoff.md just gets empty cells); it still never requires, validates, or writes front matter. `/ticket new` stamps these fields, `/ticket check` validates them, and `scripts/tickets.py` remains the sole parser and writer of front matter semantics. `tickets.py close` sets `status: done` and stamps `from: <id>` on each follow-up idea ticket it creates. `board.py` also uses ticket status to decide which tasks it lists at all: a `dropped` ticket, or a `done` ticket with no recorded step work, is left off the board entirely.
103	
104	`status` here is a person's decision (proposed, ready to build, blocked, done, dropped), not build progress. It never tracks how far a task got through the roles; that stays derived by `/board` from `.sdlc/` run state. The two are independent: a ticket can sit at `status: ready` while `/board` shows no runs yet, or `status: blocked` while a step has already built.
105	
106	Origin: this convention comes from the `.sdlc/_templates/` and `CONTEXT.md` of the gen-ui-system-svelte-lite project. The ticket templates this plugin ships are in `skills/ticket/templates/`.
107	
108	## Task handoff (`.sdlc/<task>/handoff.md`)
109	
110	```
111	## Goal
112	One or two sentences: the outcome, not the method.
113	
114	## Intent
115	Written by /clarify: literal ask, deltas, do, non-goals, done when. Optional.
116	
117	## Context
118	Decisions already made, relevant paths, links. Point to `design.md` and `decompose/report.md` when they exist. Everything a clean-context agent needs; it sees nothing else.
119	
120	## Constraints
121	What must not change, limits, deadlines. "None" if none.
122	
123	## Question
124	Only for scout, archaeologist, or researcher runs: the exact question.
125	
126	## Plan review
127	Optional. Written by /chain or the conductor, never by a role: a plan defect found before or during the build, quoting the `steps.py split` refusal or the role's `plan defect:` note, or a `recurring finding:` entry quoting both notes of a finding that repeated after it was addressed. A criterion swap adds one line, `swap applied: step <n>: <steps.py swap stdout line>`, and a swap refusal adds the `steps.py swap` stderr (its last line starts `plan defect:`) before the replan. A scope widening (/chain 4.9) adds `scope widened: step <n>: <steps.py widen stdout line>`; a `steps.py widen` refusal adds `scope decision: step <n>: <paths>` and its stderr before the replan. A plan review whose Verdict is `replan` (`steps.py review` prints `replan`, /chain 3) adds `plan review: replan: <result path>` and one `plan review: <verdict>: <finding>` entry per item of the reviewer's `## Findings`, before the planner L3 replan. Earlier entries stay. The planner fixes that step on the replan.
128	```
129	
130	## Step handoff (`.sdlc/<task>/step-<n>/handoff.md`)
131	
132	`scripts/steps.py split` writes these files from the newest planner file. /chain 5 writes the `Loose ends` step handoff (`step-<n+1>/`) by hand from the same template and lints it with `steps.py lint`, and so does `/fix` for its single `step-1/`. `steps.py swap` is the one other writer: it rewrites one criterion line from the verifier's `swap old:`/`swap new:` pair after a `plan defect:` fail (/chain 4.8), never by hand. `steps.py widen` widens the scope criterion with conductor-allowed paths (/chain 4.9) and appends one item per path to a `## Scope widened` section at the end of the step handoff: ``- `<path>`: allowed by a conductor scope decision (steps.py widen)``.
133	
134	A plan may hold a `guard timeout: <seconds>` line (in `## Goal` for the whole plan, or right after a step's `level:` line for that step); `steps.py split --only` uses it as the `--guard-timeout` default, an explicit `--guard-timeout` wins, and `specgate.py check` refuses a `(guard)` that runs `check.sh` without one.
135	
136	Copied from the plan's step block, plus the task goal for orientation:
137	
138	```
139	## Task goal
140	<from the task handoff>
141	
142	## Step <n>: <title>
143	level: L<n>
144	### Read first
145	- `<path>`
146	
147	### Do
148	...
149	
150	### Acceptance criteria
151	- ...
152	```
153	
154	`### Read first` is optional. For each file the step changes, it lists the nearest `AGENTS.md` in that file's folder or a folder above it, leaving out the root entry, one ``- `<path>` `` line each, relative to the repository root. A step whose only entry is the root has no `### Read first`. `steps.py lint` refuses a listed path that does not exist.
155	
156	### Merge step
157	
158	When a task merges one lane into another, the planner emits this block (from `agents/planner.md`, `## Merge steps`) with `<branch>`, `<n>`, and `<gate command>` filled in, and `steps.py split` copies it like any other step:
159	
160	```merge-step
161	## Step <n>: Merge <branch>
162	level: L<n>
163	### Do
164	Run `git merge --no-ff <branch>` on a tree with no uncommitted tracked changes. Resolve every conflict so both lanes' intent survives, run the gates below, and create the merge commit. Never push.
165	### Acceptance criteria
166	- `test "$(git rev-list --parents -n1 HEAD | wc -w)" -eq 3`
167	- `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> HEAD`
168	- (guard) `! git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD`
169	- (guard) `out=$(git diff-tree --cc HEAD) && ! printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -qE "^\+\+(<<<<<<<|>>>>>>>)( |$)"`
170	- (guard) `<gate command>` shows no new findings versus the first parent: run the same command in a `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD^1` copy and compare.
171	```
172	
173	The conflict-marker guard flags only `++` lines of `git diff-tree --cc HEAD`, so a kept marker line textually identical to a parent line that aligns with it (shown as `+ ` or ` +`) passes. This is accepted, because no one-line guard separates it from a legit lane line in a file both sides changed. The builder must still resolve every conflict, and the check.py probe pins the miss.
174	
175	`## Previous attempt` is appended by /chain 4.4 only after a verifier fail that is not a plan defect (its For the next attempt does not start with `plan defect:`). A blocked builder or a `plan defect:` fail goes to a replan instead, and the step handoff is rewritten by `steps.py split`, not appended to. A swapped plan defect (a `plan defect:` fail whose criterion `steps.py swap` replaced) rebuilds at the same level without `## Previous attempt`.
176	
177	## Batched verifier result (task dir)
178	
179	A verifier launched at the task dir writes `verifier-L<k>.md` in the task dir, not in a step dir. After `## For the next attempt` it adds a `## Verified` section with one item per builder result it verified, the path relative to the task dir, bare or in a code span:
180	
181	```
182	## Verified
183	- step-<n>/builder-L<k>[-j].md
184	```
185	
186	`steps.py next` and `resume` treat a listed step as verified while the listed path is still that step's newest builder result by `order.py` (a rebuild after the batch is not listed, so the step goes back to `verify`), and `board.py` renders it. The newest task-dir verifier result (by `order.py`) that lists the build decides: it counts only with Verdict `pass` and no `results.structure_error`, so a later `fail` on the same build overrides an earlier `pass`, and two batches over disjoint steps both stay valid. A step-dir verifier result that counts after the build still decides first. A step is never batch-verified when its newest builder Status is not `done`, its build is L4 or L5, its title starts with `Merge ` or holds `gates green` (any case), it is the highest-numbered live `step-<n>/` in the task dir, or a `step-<n>.superseded-<k>/` sibling exists; those steps take a per-step verifier. `## Verified` is not a declared verifier section, which is fine: `results.structure_error` ignores undeclared headings.
187	
188	## Free-text arguments
189	
190	When a launcher skill gets text instead of a handoff path, create `.sdlc/<slug>/handoff.md` (slug: 2 to 5 lowercase words from the text, hyphenated; add `-2` etc. if taken) from the template, put the text in Goal (or Question for question roles), fill Context from what the current conversation established, and show the user the path.
191

---
name: handoff-format
description: "Layout and templates for sdlc-lite task folders (.sdlc/<task>/) and handoff files. Reference for the launcher skills; not a command."
user-invocable: false
---

**Codex host:** Before following this workflow, read [the Codex adapter](../sdlc-lite/SKILL.md) and apply its tool, argument, path, and process translations. Claude Code follows the workflow below directly.

## Layout

```
.sdlc/<task-slug>/
  handoff.md            task brief (goal, intent, context, constraints)
  design.md             /grill ratified design (optional)
  decompose/            /decompose manifest-v<n>.json + report.md (optional)
  scout-L1.md           outputs of task-level roles: <role>-<level>.md
  planner-L2.md
  planner-L3-2.md       a replan; the latest runs.jsonl record is current
  plan-reviewer-L1.md   plan review (planner L3, a step at L4 or L5, a merge step, or a replan)
  runs.jsonl            one line per run: role, level, model, effort, cost, duration, file
  skips.md              lane history: one "- lane:" line per steps.py lane run, under ## Lane
                        and, under ## Skipped, one entry per full-chain role (planner, verifier
                        per step, filer) a solo, lean, or fix lane skipped (a full lane
                        needs the results instead), in the form
                        "- skip: <role>; step: <n or all>; reason: <why>; decided: <who>"
                        (reason and decided non-empty); tickets.py check and close enforce it
  step-1/
    handoff.md          one plan step: level, do, acceptance criteria
    builder-L2.md
    verifier-L1.md
  step-2/ ...
  step-2.superseded-1/   a step replaced by a replan; ignored as a step, still counted for cost
.sdlc/.NNNN-<slug>/     a closed ticket in numbered mode (renamed from NNNN-<slug> by `close`, which refuses while other files cite the old path unless `--rewrite-refs` or `--force`); same layout inside
.sdlc/roadmap.md        generated by `tickets.py roadmap`; never hand-edited
.sdlc/notes.md          follow-ups that did not become tickets, appended by `tickets.py close`; never a ticket
.sdlc/_templates/<type>.md  optional; overrides the plugin's skills/ticket/templates/<type>.md
.sdlc/AGENTS.md         router: stage counts, open tickets, and the create, claim, and close procedures; its managed block is regenerated by tickets.py roadmap, new, and close
.sdlc/CLAUDE.md         @AGENTS.md, so Claude Code loads the router
.sdlc/config            optional lines: ticket_folders: numbered, external_branch: <branch>, ticket_root: tickets
.sdlc/tickets/          the ticket folders when config has ticket_root: tickets, with its own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; roadmap.md, notes.md, config, and _templates/ stay in .sdlc/
.sdlc/runtime/          traces analysis outputs and cursor written by `traces.py` (runtime/traces/<repo-key>/); never committed
.sdlc/messages/         git-ignored mailbox written by scripts/messages.py: new/, read/, done/ per receiver, shared by worktrees; never committed; its AGENTS.md (the procedures) and CLAUDE.md at the root and in each stage folder are written by messages.py send and tickets.py roadmap
.sdlc/evals/            the plugin repository's dated model and effort evals (NNNN-<slug>.md) and table-lock.json, written by scripts/evals.py add and lock; check.py fails a model-table change that cites no newer eval; its AGENTS.md documents the format
.sdlc/proposals/        candidate changes mined from past runs (<kind>-<hash>/proposal.md, P-NNNN), written by scripts/proposals.py scan; accept needs an eval in .sdlc/evals/, promote files an idea ticket; its AGENTS.md documents the format
.sdlc/supervisor/       written by `supervisor.py init` in the main checkout: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, limits.json; hosts.local.json, state.json, status.json, lock, STOP, and wakes/ stay local
```

`scripts/run.sh <role> <level> <handoff.md>` writes `<role>-<level>.md` and `.log` next to the handoff it is given. A rerun of the same role and level writes `<role>-<level>-<k>.md` and `.log` (k = 2, 3, ...); the first result is never overwritten, and the newest is decided by `scripts/order.py`: latest runs.jsonl record (run.sh records `file`), else level then rerun index then name; never mtime. runs.jsonl keeps the history. Add `.sdlc/` to the project's `.gitignore` unless the user wants the trail committed.

A live step dir is exactly `step-<digits>`; a replan renames replaced dirs to `step-<n>.superseded-<k>/` (k is the first free number); the board and scripts do not count these as steps.

If the project commits the `.sdlc/` trail, ignore these instead so `/board` and role runs don't dirty the tree:

```
.sdlc/**/*.running
.sdlc/**/*.log
.sdlc/**/.run.lock
.sdlc/runtime/
.sdlc/messages/
.sdlc/supervisor/hosts.local.json
.sdlc/supervisor/status.json
.sdlc/supervisor/state.json
.sdlc/supervisor/lock
.sdlc/supervisor/STOP
.sdlc/supervisor/wakes/
```

- Board cache: lives in `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/sdlc-lite/board-state/`, outside the repo, so `/board` writes nothing into the tree. Ignoring `.sdlc/.board-state.json` only matters for older versions that wrote it there.
- `.sdlc/**/*.running`: marker for a role run in progress
- `.sdlc/**/*.log`: raw role transcript (stream-json: one JSON event per line, stderr mixed in)
- `.sdlc/**/.run.lock`: local lock state used to prevent overlapping runs
- `.sdlc/runtime/`: `traces.py` analysis outputs and ingest cursor, regenerated on each run
- `.sdlc/messages/`: the local mailbox written by `scripts/messages.py`; never committed, even when the trail is.

Keep the results `.md` files, `runs.jsonl`, and `*.attempt.json` committed. Attempt records preserve failed and interrupted runs even when no normal run row was written.

## Ticket front matter (optional)

In numbered mode, `close` renames the folder `NNNN-<slug>` to `.NNNN-<slug>`; tools still treat it as a closed ticket. Before the rename, `close` refuses, writing nothing, when files outside the folder cite `<root>/NNNN-<slug>` (found with `git grep`), naming each; `--rewrite-refs` rewrites them to the dot path with the rename, and `--force` closes and leaves them.

`.sdlc/<task>/handoff.md` may open with a YAML front matter block that makes the handoff double as a ticket:

```
---
id: T-NNNN
title: "..."
type: feature|bug|chore|spike|idea
status: proposed|ready|blocked|done|dropped
size: S|M|L|XL
priority: P1|P2|P3
depends: [T-NNNN, file:<path>, cap:<name>, ...]
created: YYYY-MM-DD
from: T-NNNN   # optional, origin ticket id
provides: [name, ...]   # optional, capability names this ticket delivers
claimed_by: <harness> <YYYY-MM-DD>   # optional, who works on it; shown in the router; a second claimant checks it first
router: .sdlc/AGENTS.md   # stamped by new: the folder rules (.sdlc/tickets/AGENTS.md with ticket_root: tickets)
---
```

A `file:` depends entry is repo-relative and met once the path exists; it never orders tickets. A `cap:` entry is met once a `done` ticket provides it, and orders the ticket after every provider. `check` fails a malformed entry or an unprovided `cap:`.

Front matter is purely additive: a handoff with no front matter keeps working unchanged, and `run.sh` never requires or parses it. `board.py` reads `id`/`status` from front matter for display only (via `tickets.py`'s parser, so a task without front matter or an unreadable handoff.md just gets empty cells); it still never requires, validates, or writes front matter. `/ticket new` stamps these fields, `/ticket check` validates them, and `scripts/tickets.py` remains the sole parser and writer of front matter semantics. `tickets.py close` sets `status: done` and stamps `from: <id>` on each follow-up idea ticket it creates. `board.py` also uses ticket status to decide which tasks it lists at all: a `dropped` ticket, or a `done` ticket with no recorded step work, is left off the board entirely.

`status` here is a person's decision (proposed, ready to build, blocked, done, dropped), not build progress. It never tracks how far a task got through the roles; that stays derived by `/board` from `.sdlc/` run state. The two are independent: a ticket can sit at `status: ready` while `/board` shows no runs yet, or `status: blocked` while a step has already built.

Origin: this convention comes from the `.sdlc/_templates/` and `CONTEXT.md` of the gen-ui-system-svelte-lite project. The ticket templates this plugin ships are in `skills/ticket/templates/`.

## Task handoff (`.sdlc/<task>/handoff.md`)

```
## Goal
One or two sentences: the outcome, not the method.

## Intent
Written by /clarify: literal ask, deltas, do, non-goals, done when. Optional.

## Context
Decisions already made, relevant paths, links. Point to `design.md` and `decompose/report.md` when they exist. Everything a clean-context agent needs; it sees nothing else.

## Constraints
What must not change, limits, deadlines. "None" if none.

## Question
Only for scout, archaeologist, or researcher runs: the exact question.

## Plan review
Optional. Written by /chain or the conductor, never by a role: a plan defect found before or during the build, quoting the `steps.py split` refusal or the role's `plan defect:` note, or a `recurring finding:` entry quoting both notes of a finding that repeated after it was addressed. A criterion swap adds one line, `swap applied: step <n>: <steps.py swap stdout line>`, and a swap refusal adds the `steps.py swap` stderr (its last line starts `plan defect:`) before the replan. A scope widening (/chain 4.9) adds `scope widened: step <n>: <steps.py widen stdout line>`; a `steps.py widen` refusal adds `scope decision: step <n>: <paths>` and its stderr before the replan. A plan review whose Verdict is `replan` (`steps.py review` prints `replan`, /chain 3) adds `plan review: replan: <result path>` and one `plan review: <verdict>: <finding>` entry per item of the reviewer's `## Findings`, before the planner L3 replan. Earlier entries stay. The planner fixes that step on the replan.
```

## Step handoff (`.sdlc/<task>/step-<n>/handoff.md`)

`scripts/steps.py split` writes these files from the newest planner file. /chain 5 writes the `Loose ends` step handoff (`step-<n+1>/`) by hand from the same template and lints it with `steps.py lint`, and so does `/fix` for its single `step-1/`. `steps.py swap` is the one other writer: it rewrites one criterion line from the verifier's `swap old:`/`swap new:` pair after a `plan defect:` fail (/chain 4.8), never by hand. `steps.py widen` widens the scope criterion with conductor-allowed paths (/chain 4.9) and appends one item per path to a `## Scope widened` section at the end of the step handoff: ``- `<path>`: allowed by a conductor scope decision (steps.py widen)``.

A plan may hold a `guard timeout: <seconds>` line (in `## Goal` for the whole plan, or right after a step's `level:` line for that step); `steps.py split --only` uses it as the `--guard-timeout` default, an explicit `--guard-timeout` wins, and `specgate.py check` refuses a `(guard)` that runs `check.sh` without one.

Copied from the plan's step block, plus the task goal for orientation:

```
## Task goal
<from the task handoff>

## Step <n>: <title>
level: L<n>
### Read first
- `<path>`

### Do
...

### Acceptance criteria
- ...
```

`### Read first` is optional. For each file the step changes, it lists the nearest `AGENTS.md` in that file's folder or a folder above it, leaving out the root entry, one ``- `<path>` `` line each, relative to the repository root. A step whose only entry is the root has no `### Read first`. `steps.py lint` refuses a listed path that does not exist.

### Merge step

When a task merges one lane into another, the planner emits this block (from `agents/planner.md`, `## Merge steps`) with `<branch>`, `<n>`, and `<gate command>` filled in, and `steps.py split` copies it like any other step:

```merge-step
## Step <n>: Merge <branch>
level: L<n>
### Do
Run `git merge --no-ff <branch>` on a tree with no uncommitted tracked changes. Resolve every conflict so both lanes' intent survives, run the gates below, and create the merge commit. Never push.
### Acceptance criteria
- `test "$(git rev-list --parents -n1 HEAD | wc -w)" -eq 3`
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> HEAD`
- (guard) `! git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD`
- (guard) `out=$(git diff-tree --cc HEAD) && ! printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -qE "^\+\+(<<<<<<<|>>>>>>>)( |$)"`
- (guard) `<gate command>` shows no new findings versus the first parent: run the same command in a `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD^1` copy and compare.
```

The conflict-marker guard flags only `++` lines of `git diff-tree --cc HEAD`, so a kept marker line textually identical to a parent line that aligns with it (shown as `+ ` or ` +`) passes. This is accepted, because no one-line guard separates it from a legit lane line in a file both sides changed. The builder must still resolve every conflict, and the check.py probe pins the miss.

`## Previous attempt` is appended by /chain 4.4 only after a verifier fail that is not a plan defect (its For the next attempt does not start with `plan defect:`). A blocked builder or a `plan defect:` fail goes to a replan instead, and the step handoff is rewritten by `steps.py split`, not appended to. A swapped plan defect (a `plan defect:` fail whose criterion `steps.py swap` replaced) rebuilds at the same level without `## Previous attempt`.

## Batched verifier result (task dir)

A verifier launched at the task dir writes `verifier-L<k>.md` in the task dir, not in a step dir. After `## For the next attempt` it adds a `## Verified` section with one item per builder result it verified, the path relative to the task dir, bare or in a code span:

```
## Verified
- step-<n>/builder-L<k>[-j].md
```

`steps.py next` and `resume` treat a listed step as verified while the listed path is still that step's newest builder result by `order.py` (a rebuild after the batch is not listed, so the step goes back to `verify`), and `board.py` renders it. The newest task-dir verifier result (by `order.py`) that lists the build decides: it counts only with Verdict `pass` and no `results.structure_error`, so a later `fail` on the same build overrides an earlier `pass`, and two batches over disjoint steps both stay valid. A step-dir verifier result that counts after the build still decides first. A step is never batch-verified when its newest builder Status is not `done`, its build is L4 or L5, its title starts with `Merge ` or holds `gates green` (any case), it is the highest-numbered live `step-<n>/` in the task dir, or a `step-<n>.superseded-<k>/` sibling exists; those steps take a per-step verifier. `## Verified` is not a declared verifier section, which is fine: `results.structure_error` ignores undeclared headings.

## Free-text arguments

When a launcher skill gets text instead of a handoff path, create `.sdlc/<slug>/handoff.md` (slug: 2 to 5 lowercase words from the text, hyphenated; add `-2` etc. if taken) from the template, put the text in Goal (or Question for question roles), fill Context from what the current conversation established, and show the user the path.

In an interactive session: a role or a full /chain can take 15 to 30 minutes, past the Bash tool's 10-minute cap, so run `run.sh` with `run_in_background: true` and wait for the completion notification. Never poll with `sleep`. Once notified, read `<role>-<level>.md`. Ending the turn is safe here because the notification re-invokes the session.
31-- Planner, builder, and verifier work runs only through `run.sh`. Never spawn an agent through the Agent tool in their place: not another plugin's builder, planner, reviewer, or checker agent, and not SDLC Lite's own role agents. Other plugins' agents are not substitutes, even when they are listed as proactive. In Claude Code, `hooks/block-role-spawn.sh` denies such spawns; Codex has no equivalent enforcement.
32:- Levels follow the level-rubric skill. After every builder and verifier run, the next action comes from `steps.py next <step dir>`. Escalation follows /chain: builder blocked → replan (never verify a blocked build); verifier with no verdict → `reverify` at the same level, never counted as a fail, and a second in a row → stop; verifier fail → rebuild once with its notes, a second fail → up one level; L5 fail → stop and ask the user; builder Status `inherited red: <tests>` or verifier Verdict `inherited red: <tests>` (`steps.py next` prints `inherited`: the gate was already red at the pre-build HEAD) → interactive, ask the user through AskUserQuestion (fix main first, rebuild once main is green, or stop), unattended, stop the task and report the inherited tests; it is never a fail, a rebuild, a bump, a replan, or a reverify, and never waives the gate. A `plan defect:` note from the builder or the verifier, or a `steps.py split` refusal naming a `plan defect`, means a planner L3 replan, never a rebuild or a level bump, except that `steps.py next` printing `swap` (a verifier plan defect with one `swap old:`/`swap new:` pair, the first on the step) means `steps.py swap <step dir>`, then the builder at the printed level with no `## Previous attempt`; a swap refusal is a plan defect and goes to a planner L3 replan; a swap is never a bump. A builder blocked only because a file it needs sits outside the step's scope criterion, when the conductor decides the file serves the task goal (interactive: confirm through AskUserQuestion), means `steps.py widen <step dir> <path>...` (/chain 4.9), never prose alone: exit 0 → append `scope widened: step <n>: <stdout line>` to `## Plan review` and rerun the builder at the same level, no bump, no `## Previous attempt`, not counted toward a bump; exit 1 → append `scope decision: step <n>: <paths>` and the stderr to `## Plan review` and replan. A recurring finding (same criterion, same root cause as an earlier attempt on the step, after it was addressed) means a planner L3 replan that questions the plan or rule, never a level bump.
33-- A plan goes through `steps.py review <task dir>` before `steps.py split`: `review L1` runs the plan-reviewer through `run.sh` (never the Agent tool); `replan` appends its findings as `plan review: replan: <finding>` lines to `## Plan review` and replans at planner L3; `stop` asks the user (a `blocked` verdict names its `## Missing decisions`; a second `replan` stops). Routine plans get no review. A `run.sh plan-reviewer` exit 2 with `specgate:` lines is a `specgate.py check` refusal; /chain 3 routes it as a plan defect.
34-- Follow-ups carry the filer's tags. `fix-now:` runs in /chain's `Loose ends` step; `decide:` is asked once in the close-out round, and at most one becomes a ticket through `tickets.py close --ticket N`; `note:` goes to `.sdlc/notes.md`. Never file a follow-up ticket any other way.
35-- A `run.sh` exit 3 means the role ended without its required section; it goes through `steps.py next`, never to done.
36-- Every other Agent-tool spawn, such as a read-only search helper, states `model` per the "Agent-tool spawns" section of the level-rubric skill.
37-- Publishing (commit, push, PR, issue) happens only after the user approves it through AskUserQuestion.
38:- `hooks/block-publish.sh` exits 0 unless `SDLC_ROLE` is set, `scripts/run.sh` sets it per role run, and `scripts/fanout.py` sets it to `conductor` for every lane driver, so a lane conductor is guarded. An interactive session has no `SDLC_ROLE`, so the hook does not apply to it. Publishing from this session is gated only by the AskUserQuestion approval above.
39-
40-## Skips and stops
41-- Record every skip in the task's `skips.md`. A skip the lane script does not permit needs the user's approval through AskUserQuestion before it is recorded.
42-- Never skipped: the independent verifier on L4 or L5 and merge steps, the required plan review, a focused live run for a role behavior change, the filer when follow-ups or warnings were reported, and user approval for any publish.
43-- Batch plan reviews across a fanout run on one model family. Run one `/sdlc-lite:open-questions` round per ticket set. Run independent tickets in parallel fanout lanes.
44-- Stop rules: a second `replan` verdict, or a ticket past its budget once the budget ticket lands, is a hard stop that comes to the user.
45-
46-## Stay thin
